newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debts defy U.S. Treasuries to end higher.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debts defy U.S. Treasuries to end higher.

text.p: Emerging market debts staged a follow through rally on Wedensday but ended off the day's highs, traders said.

Positive sentiments from two major developments on Tuesday -- that a score or so Argentine companies got upgraded and the Peruvian hostage crisis was finally brought to an end -- continued supporting Latin assets, traders said.
The bid tone lasted for the good part of the day, but the weakness of the Treasuries finally took the toll late in the session, they said.
"The upgrade of so many Argentine companies gave hope that the sovereign rating would soon be lifted to investment grade," said a trader with a European bank.

Argentine sovereign credit was raised to double B from double B minus by Standard and Poor's on April 2. It is two notches below investment grade. The Moody's Investors Service left its B1 rating unchanged.
Argentina FRBs rose 3/4 to 90-5/8, but Argentina Global -17, which jumped 1-3/8 on Tuesday, slipped 1/8 to 104-1/4 bid.
The momentum on Peru's rally was short-lived. Its PDI bond slipped 1/8 to 58-1/8.
"It was a dealer's market," said another trader. "There was little outside interest."
The light volume notwithstanding, traders were upbeat that the spreads on emerging debts appeared to have found a bottom.
"Even if the Treasuries still try to price in another Fed funds rate increase, spreads of Latin debts would widen at most 10 to 15 basis points," the trader said.
